mainTopic: Calculations on שבת, the משנה of אין מחשיכין, רב יהודה's rule about speaking of plans that have a permitted version, working before הבדלה, and אבא שאול's general rule
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about calculations on שבת and settles a contradiction with a second ברייתא. Counting past expenses is forbidden only when wages are still owed, because then the counting has a practical use. The גמרא then turns to the משנה of אין מחשיכין. It tells the story of a חסיד who would not fix his fence because he had thought about fixing it on שבת, and a caper bush grew in the gap and supported his family. רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that you may speak on שבת about a trip planned for after שבת, because with בורגנין the walk itself would be permitted. The גמרא tests this rule against the משנה, a ברייתא of רבי אושעיא, and a ברייתא about a bride and a dead person. Each time it answers that the case has no permitted version on שבת: attached fruit, rotten hay, and cutting myrtle or cloth. Next the גמרא asks how one may guard his field at nightfall before הבדלה. It answers either that he stands among winepresses where wine is available, or that saying 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול' is enough to begin work. Finally, the גמרא begins to ask which clause of the משנה אבא שאול's general rule refers to, and this question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pointless calculations are allowed on שבת
steps.stepSummary: This is the last line of a ברייתא quoted on the previous amud. It says that calculations with no real purpose may be done on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And calculations of 'what does it matter' (things that make no practical difference) are allowed to be calculated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting earlier. This last line says that calculations with no practical use are permitted on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier lines of this ברייתא forbade calculations about what was already spent and what will be spent in the future. This closing line adds that 'meaningless' calculations, which change nothing in real life, are fine. Keep this ברייתא in mind, because the next step will set another source against it.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'of what is in this?' Something of no real significance or practical use.
To calculate them (to do the accounting).
Calculations, accounts.

phrases.english: And those of 'what does it matter' (no practical significance)
phrases.notes: This is the tail end of a ברייתא that began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: are permitted to calculate them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calculations with no practical significance are permitted on שבת.

steps.title: A second ברייתא allows counting past expenses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא that allows a person to state his past expenses on שבת. This seems to contradict the first ברייתא, which forbade calculating 'what was'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradicted it: One may make calculations that are not needed, but one may not make calculations that are needed, on שבת. How so? A person may say to his friend: 'I spent such-and-such number of workers on this field, I spent such-and-such number of דינרים on this house.' But he may not say to him: 'I spent such-and-such, and I will spend such-and-such in the future.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a second ברייתא against the first one. The second ברייתא allows talking about money already spent, while the first ברייתא forbade it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said calculations of 'what was' (past expenses) are forbidden. The second ברייתא calls past expenses 'unneeded' calculations and permits them; only a mix of past and future planning is forbidden. So the two sources disagree about past expenses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contradicted it.' The גמרא is setting one source against another.
Needed, having practical use.
Workers, hired laborers.
דינרים, coins.
Will spend in the future.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second ברייתא forbids talking about money entirely. It allows talking about past spending and only forbids adding future plans, which turns the talk into practical business planning.

phrases.english: And they contradicted it: One may calculate calculations that are not needed,
but one may not calculate calculations that are needed, on Shabbat.
How so? A person may say to his friend:

phrases.aramaic: ״כָּךְ וְכָךְ פּוֹעֲלִים הוֹצֵאתִי עַל שָׂדֶה זוֹ,
phrases.english: 'Such-and-such number of workers I spent on this field,'

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ וְכָךְ דִּינָרִין הוֹצֵאתִי עַל דִּירָה זוֹ״.
phrases.english: 'such-and-such number of dinars I spent on this house.'
But he may not say to him:
'Such-and-such I have spent,'
'and such-and-such I am going to spend in the future!'
phrases.notes: The exclamation shows that the גמרא is pointing out a contradiction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא completed in step 1 by quoting a conflicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's ban on calculating past expenses ('what was').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second ברייתא explicitly permits stating past expenses on שבת, which directly conflicts with the first ברייתא forbidding it.

steps.title: The first ברייתא already contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא replies that even without the second ברייתא, the first ברייתא is hard to understand on its own terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, the first ברייתא itself is difficult for you!
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא points out a deeper problem: the first ברייתא seems to contradict itself. This prepares the way for one answer that will solve both problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא forbids calculating past expenses, yet it permits pointless calculations. But past expenses are already finished, so counting them should itself count as pointless. The גמרא is saying that the real question is what 'past expenses' means in the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And according to your reasoning.' Following the asker's own logic.
'It itself.' The source is difficult on its own terms.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, it itself is difficult for you!
phrases.notes: The first ברייתא seems to contradict itself: past expenses are forbidden, yet 'meaningless' calculations are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the contradiction in step 2 by showing that the first ברייתא has an internal difficulty that must be solved first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Past expenses seem to have no practical significance, so forbidding them clashes with permitting 'של מה בכך' calculations.

steps.title: It depends on whether wages are still owed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves everything. The ברייתא that forbids counting past expenses is talking about a case where the person still owes his workers wages. The ברייתא that permits it is talking about a case where nothing is owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: this ברייתא (which forbids) is where he still has the workers' wages with him (unpaid). That ברייתא (which permits) is where he does not have the workers' wages with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two ברייתות are talking about different situations. The key is whether the person still owes money to his hired workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wages are still owed, counting past expenses has a real use: it tells him how much he must pay. So it is a 'needed' calculation and is forbidden. If everything is already paid, the counting changes nothing, so it is like של מה בכך and is permitted. This one distinction fixes both the contradiction between the ברייתות and the inner problem in the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' This introduces the real answer.
'This ... that.' Each source is applied to a different case.
The wages of the hired worker.
With him (still in his possession, not yet paid).

steps.whatToRemember: A calculation on שבת is forbidden when it has real, practical use, such as working out wages still owed. Counting past expenses that are already settled is permitted, because it is like של מה בכך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the working rule for talking about money on שבת. The test is not past versus future. The test is whether the calculation has any practical use right now.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: הָא — דְּאִיכָּא אַגְרָא דַאֲגִירָא גַּבֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Rather: this is where there is the hired worker's wage still with him.
phrases.notes: This refers to the first ברייתא, which forbids. The calculation is practical because money is still owed.

phrases.english: That is where there is no hired worker's wage still with him.
phrases.notes: This refers to the second ברייתא, which permits. Nothing is owed, so the calculation is meaningless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּאִיכָּא אַגְרָא דַאֲגִירָא גַּבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both the contradiction in step 2 and the internal difficulty in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is applied to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calculating past expenses is always the same act, so the sources truly conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Past expenses are forbidden to calculate only when wages are still owed (a practical use). When everything is settled, it is permitted as של מה בכך.

steps.title: A pious man refuses to fix his fence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, אין מחשיכין, and quotes a ברייתא story. A חסיד thought about fencing a breach in his field on שבת, then remembered it was שבת and chose never to fix it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may not wait for nightfall' (from the משנה). The רבנן taught: There was a story with a certain חסיד. A breach opened in the fence of his field, and he decided to fence it in. Then he remembered that it was שבת, and that חסיד held back and did not fence it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's words אין מחשיכין, then tells a story about a חסיד. This step sets up the story; the next step gives its miraculous ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids preparing on שבת for weekday work, such as waiting at the תחום to start work right after שבת. The חסיד went even further: because he had only thought about fixing the fence on שבת, he refused to ever fix it. The story shows how seriously he guarded שבת, even in his thoughts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One may not wait for nightfall' (from the משנה). One may not wait at the תחום edge on שבת in order to do weekday business right after שבת.
A pious person who goes beyond the letter of the law.
A breach, a gap in a fence.
And he decided, he thought it over.

steps.confusionAlert: The חסיד did not fix the fence even after שבת. He refused to fix it forever, because he had thought about it on שבת. That is why he is called a חסיד: he went beyond what the law requires.

phrases.english: 'One may not wait for nightfall.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה to start the new discussion.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: There was an incident with a certain pious man
in whose field a breach was broken open,
and he decided to fence it in,
and he remembered that it was Shabbat,
and that pious man held back and did not fence it (ever),

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַחְשִׁיכִין תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן מַעֲשֶׂה בְּחָסִיד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה (אין מחשיכין), unrelated to the calculations discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חסיד refrains from acting on weekday plans he thought about on שבת, even beyond the letter of the law.

steps.title: A miracle rewards the pious man
steps.stepSummary: Because he guarded שבת, a miracle happened. A caper bush grew in the breach, closing the gap, and its fruit supported him and his whole family.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a miracle was done for him: a caper bush grew up in it (the breach), and from it came his livelihood and the livelihood of the members of his household.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the reward. A caper bush grew in the gap and closed the fence, and its produce fed the חסיד's whole family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חסיד gave up fixing the fence, which looked like a loss. Instead the gap was sealed by nature and became a source of income. The message is that honoring שבת, even in one's thoughts, brings blessing rather than loss.

keyTerms.meaning: A miracle.
A caper bush (a thorny plant with edible buds and fruit).
Livelihood, financial support.
The members of his household (his family).

steps.whatToRemember: The story of the חסיד teaches that guarding שבת even in thought, and giving up work one planned on שבת, is rewarded. His loss became his livelihood.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story supports the spirit of the משנה of אין מחשיכין: on שבת one should keep away from weekday work and plans. The גמרא then turns to רב יהודה's rule about when one may speak on שבת about plans for after שבת.

phrases.english: and a miracle was done for him,
and a caper bush grew up in it (the breach),
and from it came his livelihood
and the livelihood of the members of his household.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַעֲשָׂה לוֹ נֵס וְעָלְתָה בּוֹ צָלָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 5 with the miraculous reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Refraining from weekday work for the sake of שבת leads to blessing: the חסיד's breach was sealed by a caper bush that became his livelihood.

steps.title: You may talk about a trip that could have been allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that you may tell a friend on שבת that you are traveling to a city tomorrow, because with בורגנין the walk would be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A person may say to his friend, 'I am going to such-and-such city tomorrow.' This is allowed because if there were guardhouses along the way, he would be allowed to walk there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule. You may talk on שבת about doing something after שבת if there is some situation where that thing itself could be done on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking far past the תחום is normally forbidden on שבת. But if there were small guardhouses (בורגנין) along the road, the whole area would count as one settled place, and the walk would be allowed. Since the act is permitted in at least one situation, talking about it is allowed even when the guardhouses are not there.

keyTerms.meaning: A large walled city
Such-and-such, so-and-so
Small guardhouses along a road. They join the area into one settlement for the rules of תחום
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the yardstick for the rest of the sugya. Every later challenge asks whether a forbidden case has 'a permitted version' like the בורגנין.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
A person is permitted to say to his friend
'To such-and-such city I am going tomorrow,'
for if there were guardhouses, he could walk.
phrases.notes: The guardhouses would make the walk itself permitted on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of the חסיד, the גמרא brings a halachic rule. The rule shows when talking about weekday plans on שבת is allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking on שבת about an act is permitted if that act could be done on שבת in some permitted situation (here, with בורגנין).

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about bringing fruit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids waiting at the תחום to bring fruit. But by שמואל's logic it should be allowed, since with partitions you could bring fruit even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: one may not wait for nightfall at the edge of the תחום to hire workers or to bring fruit. Hiring workers makes sense, since you can never hire on שבת. But bringing fruit? Let us say: since if there were partitions there he could bring it, it should be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's rule from our משנה. Hiring workers is fine, but the ban on bringing fruit seems to go against the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hiring workers is never allowed on שבת, so waiting in order to hire fits the rule. Fruit is different. If partitions surrounded the area, carrying the fruit would be permitted. So by the logic of the בורגנין, waiting at the תחום to bring fruit should be allowed, yet the משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: The שבת boundary, beyond which one may not walk
It makes sense regarding (first half of a 'this is fine, but that is hard' question)
Partitions or walls that enclose an area
Let us say (proposing a reasoning)

phrases.english: We learned: One may not wait for nightfall at the Shabbat boundary
to hire workers or to bring fruit.
It makes sense regarding hiring workers,
since on Shabbat one cannot hire at all,
but to bring fruit, why not?

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא: שֶׁאִם יֵשׁ שָׁם מְחִיצּוֹת — מֵבִיא!
phrases.english: Let us say: since if there were partitions there, he could bring it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב יהודה's rule against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל (step 7)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fruit can be carried on שבת if partitions are present. By the בורגנין logic, waiting to bring it should be allowed, yet the משנה forbids it.

steps.title: The משנה means fruit still attached to the tree
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's fruit is still attached to the ground. Picking it is never allowed on שבת, so there is no permitted version.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can find such a case with fruit that is still attached to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about fruit still growing on the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking fruit is forbidden on שבת no matter what. Partitions do not help. Since there is no permitted way to do this act on שבת, the rule of the בורגנין does not apply, and the משנה fits רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it (a case where it works)
Attached to the ground, still growing

phrases.english: You can find it with fruit that is attached to the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's fruit is already picked, so partitions would make carrying it permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's fruit is still attached. No permitted version exists, so the ban fits רב יהודה.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי אושעיא about hay
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא forbids waiting at the תחום to bring hay and straw. Straw can be attached, but hay is already cut, so why is it forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אושעיא taught: one may not wait for nightfall at the edge of the תחום to bring hay and straw. Straw makes sense, since you can find it attached to the ground. But hay, how can you find a case where it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב יהודה from a ברייתא of רבי אושעיא. The straw part works, but the hay part seems hard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straw can still be standing in the field, like the attached fruit of step 9. Hay is already cut. With partitions, it could be carried on שבת, so the 'attached' answer cannot explain why waiting to bring hay is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introducing a contradicting ברייתא)
Hay, already cut and detached
Straw or stalks, which can still be attached
How can you find a case for it?

phrases.english: But Rabbi Oshaya taught:
One may not wait for nightfall at the Shabbat boundary
to bring hay and straw.
It makes sense regarding straw: you can find it attached.
But hay, how can you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב יהודה. The 'attached' answer of step 9 cannot work for hay.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל (step 7), as defended in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hay is already detached and could be carried with partitions. So the ban on waiting to bring it contradicts the בורגנין rule.

steps.title: The hay is rotten and therefore מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא means rotten hay. It is מוקצה and can never be carried on שבת, even with partitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: With rotten hay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אושעיא is talking about rotten hay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rotten hay is not fit even for animals, so it is מוקצה. Partitions do not help, because the problem is not the place but the item itself. With no permitted version, the ban fits רב יהודה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rotten hay
An item set aside that may not be moved on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Talking or waiting on שבת is permitted only if the act has some permitted version (like בורגנין or partitions). Attached fruit, attached straw, and rotten (מוקצה) hay have no permitted version, so waiting for them stays forbidden.

phrases.english: With rotten hay.
phrases.notes: Rotten hay is מוקצה, so it may not be carried even within partitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hay is normal, usable hay that partitions would allow you to carry.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hay is rotten and מוקצה. No permitted version exists, so רב יהודה's rule stands.

steps.title: New challenge: waiting is allowed only for a bride or the dead
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows waiting at the תחום only for the needs of a bride or a dead person. This implies it is forbidden for anything else, which seems to go against רב יהודה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One may wait for nightfall at the edge of the תחום to take care of the needs of a bride and the needs of a dead person. For a bride or a dead person, yes. For other matters, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source to test רב יהודה's rule. This step only sets up the challenge; the גמרא will explain the problem next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says waiting at the תחום is allowed for a bride or a funeral. The inference is that for anyone else's needs it is forbidden. If בורגנין make talking and waiting allowed, why limit this to a bride and the dead? The גמרא will next ask what exact case the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: To take care of, attend to
The needs of a bride (wedding preparations)
The needs of a dead person (burial preparations)
Yes... no (an inference from the wording)

steps.confusionAlert: Here מחשיכין appears without אין, so it is permitted. This is the opposite of the earlier lines. Read the opening word carefully.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One may wait for nightfall at the Shabbat boundary
to attend to the needs of a bride
and to the needs of a dead person.
For the needs of a bride or a dead person, yes;
for the needs of something else, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַחְשִׁיכִין עַל הַתְּחוּם לְפַקֵּחַ עַל עִסְקֵי כַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב יהודה twice, the גמרא brings a new source to test the rule again.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל (step 7)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows waiting only for a bride or the dead, which implies it is forbidden for other needs. That seems to clash with the idea that a possible permitted version (בורגנין) makes it allowed. The full argument continues next.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא allows things for a dead person but not for others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא's cases: for a bride, cutting myrtle; for a dead person, bringing a coffin and shrouds. Only the dead person is allowed, and anyone else is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for 'another person' like a bride, you can find a case: cutting myrtle for him. But for a dead person, what is the case? Bringing him a coffin and shrouds. And the ברייתא teaches: for a dead person, yes; for someone else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is sharpening the question from step 12. It spells out exactly what the ברייתא means for the bride and for the dead person, and gets ready to attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting myrtle is never allowed on שבת, so the bride case fits רב יהודה's rule without trouble. But bringing a coffin and shrouds is just carrying. With partitions it would be allowed on שבת. Yet the ברייתא says it is allowed only for a dead person, not for anyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part is fine
Myrtle (cut for a bride's celebration)
Coffin
Burial shrouds
Another person (anyone besides the bride or the dead person)

phrases.english: Granted, 'another' similar to a bride
you can find a case: to cut him a myrtle.
phrases.notes: Cutting a plant is forbidden on שבת in every situation.

phrases.english: But a dead person, what is the case?
To bring him a coffin and shrouds.
And it teaches: a dead person, yes,
but another person, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds out the challenge begun in step 12 by defining the dead-person case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that one may wait at the תחום for anything that could be brought with partitions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Coffin and shrouds could be carried with partitions, yet the ברייתא allows this only for a dead person.

steps.title: Partitions should make it allowed for anyone
steps.stepSummary: Why is it forbidden for other people? By רב יהודה's logic, since it could be brought with partitions, it should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let us say: since if there were partitions there he could bring it, so he may wait for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states its attack openly. By רב יהודה's rule, waiting to bring these things should be allowed for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said that whatever has a permitted version on שבת (with partitions) may be waited for at the תחום. Carrying a coffin has such a version. So the ברייתא's limit to a dead person seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: And why?
Let us say
He may bring

phrases.english: And why?
Let us say: since if there were partitions there
he may bring it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל (step 7), whose partition rule clashes with the ברייתא's limit to a dead person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying רב יהודה's partition rule, bringing a coffin should be allowed for anyone.

steps.title: The dead-person case means cutting cloth for shrouds
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's dead-person case is cutting a cloak to make shrouds. That can never be done on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a dead person too, you can find a case: cutting a cloak for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. The ברייתא is not talking about carrying. It means cutting cloth for shrouds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting cloth is forbidden on שבת even with partitions, so רב יהודה's rule does not apply to it. Waiting at the תחום for it is allowed only because caring for a dead person is a מצוה. So the ברייתא and רב יהודה do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloak or garment (cut to make shrouds)
To cut

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of bride and dead person speaks only of acts that are never allowed on שבת (cutting myrtle, cutting cloth). רב יהודה's rule stands.

phrases.english: With a dead person too, you can find a case
to cut a cloak for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about carrying a coffin and shrouds, which has a permitted version.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about cutting cloth, which has no permitted version on שבת.

steps.title: How can he work before making הבדלה?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one may wait at the תחום to guard his produce. But he would then be working before הבדלה, which רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But one may wait for nightfall.' Even though he has not made הבדלה? But רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: a person may not do his business before he makes הבדלה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new phrase from the משנה, 'אבל מחשיכין', and challenges it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Watching a field right after שבת is weekday activity. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbids doing your own business before הבדלה. So how can the משנה let him start at nightfall?

keyTerms.meaning: Waiting until dark (at the edge of the תחום)
Made הבדלה
His personal business or needs

phrases.english: But one may wait for nightfall.
Even though he did not make havdala?
But didn't Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonos say
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
It is forbidden for a person to do his business
before he makes havdala!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אַבְדֵּיל וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new phrase of the משנה and opens a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling 'אבל מחשיכין' (one may wait to guard produce)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Guarding the field starts right at nightfall, before any הבדלה, and that is forbidden.

steps.title: הבדלה in prayer alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: Maybe he made הבדלה in the עמידה prayer? No. שמואל says one who does that must still make הבדלה over a cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he made הבדלה in prayer, but didn't רב יהודה say in the name of שמואל: one who makes הבדלה in prayer must still make הבדלה over a cup!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible answer, that he said הבדלה in his prayer, and then knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested answer is that the הבדלה in the עמידה ('אתה חוננתנו') was enough. But שמואל rules that a cup is still needed. So the question stays: he still has not fully made הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a suggested answer)
Prayer (the עמידה)
Cup (of wine, for הבדלה)

phrases.english: And if you say he made havdala in prayer
But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Shmuel:
One who makes havdala in prayer
must still make havdala over the cup!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and rejects a possible answer to step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested answer that הבדלה in prayer is enough
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל requires הבדלה over a cup even after הבדלה in prayer.

steps.title: There is no cup of wine in the field
steps.stepSummary: Maybe he made הבדלה over a cup? But who has a cup of wine out in the field?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he made הבדלה over a cup, is there a cup in the field?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second possible answer and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is standing at the edge of the תחום, far out in the fields. He would not have wine with him. So he could not have made הבדלה over a cup, and the question is even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Field
Is there? (implying: of course not)

phrases.english: And if you say he made havdala over a cup,
is there a cup in the field?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the next possible answer after step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested answer that he made הבדלה over a cup
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No wine is normally available in the field.

steps.title: The משנה is about a field among winepresses
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר אמי explains that the משנה speaks of a תחום edge among winepresses, so wine was there for הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן בר אמי explained it before רבא: they taught this among the winepresses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. The משנה describes a special place where wine is close by.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the edge of the תחום is among winepresses, he can take wine and make הבדלה over a cup. Then he is not working before הבדלה. The משנה is set in this specific case.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it
Winepresses
They taught (the ruling was taught about)

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan bar Ami explained it
before Rava:
They taught it among the winepresses.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמָא רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר אַמֵּי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 16 to 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He is in an open field with no wine, so he works before הבדלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is among winepresses and makes הבדלה over wine first.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל a short blessing is enough to start working
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא tells רב אשי that in ארץ ישראל they say 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול' and then do their work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רב אשי: in the West we say this: 'Who distinguishes between holy and mundane,' and then we do our needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. You do not need a cup to start working. Saying a short phrase of separation is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against working before הבדלה is satisfied by saying 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול'. The full הבדלה over a cup can come later. So the person in the field can say this phrase and start guarding, with no wine needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The West, meaning ארץ ישראל
'Who distinguishes between holy and mundane', a short phrase of separation
Our needs or work

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel הבדלה over a cup. It only means the short phrase is enough to permit starting work. The cup הבדלה is still made later.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi:
In the West we say this:
'Who distinguishes between holy and mundane'
and we do our needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרִינַן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 16 than the winepress answer of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what counts as הבדלה for permitting work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only הבדלה over a cup allows a person to start working.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saying 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול' is enough to start working.

steps.title: רב כהנא's household did the same
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רב כהנא would say 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול' and then they would cut wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: when I was in the house of רב כהנא, he would say 'Who distinguishes between holy and mundane,' and we would cut wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי backs up רבי אבא's answer with what he saw in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting wood is real weekday work, and they did it right after saying the short phrase. This shows the practice was followed in בבל too, not only in ארץ ישראל. It supports the answer that the person guarding his field may start after this phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: The house (study hall) of רב כהנא
We would cut wood chips

steps.whatToRemember: How can one guard his field right after שבת? Either he is among winepresses and makes הבדלה over wine, or saying 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול' is enough to permit work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that saying 'ברוך המבדיל בין קודש לחול' allows one to do מלאכה on מוצאי שבת before הבדלה over a cup.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When I was in the house of Rav Kahana
he would say 'Who distinguishes between holy and mundane'
and we would cut wood chips.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי כִּי הֲוֵינָא בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבא's answer in step 20 with a practice from בבל.
steps.raayaObject: That saying 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול' is enough to permit work
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice in רב כהנא's house, reported by רב אשי

steps.title: Quoting אבא שאול's general rule from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of אבא שאול's rule in the משנה so it can discuss it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: אבא שאול said a general rule: 'Anything that I am [allowed to talk about on שבת, I may wait at the edge of the תחום for it]', and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה to start a new discussion. It is setting up the question that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, אבא שאול gives a broad rule. If something is allowed to be said on שבת, a person may also go wait at the edge of the תחום on שבת so he can do it right when שבת ends. The גמרא gives only the first few words (וכו׳) because the learner already knows the rest of the line.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the quote continues

steps.whyThisMatters: אבא שאול's rule links two things: what you may say on שבת and what you may prepare for on שבת. The rest of the sugya tries to work out exactly what this rule is built on.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul stated a general rule:
Anything that I am [permitted to discuss], etc.
phrases.notes: The whole line reads: anything I'm permitted to say, I may wait at the edge of the boundary for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הבדלה discussion and moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything one is permitted to say on שבת, one may wait at the edge of the תחום for it.

steps.title: Which clause does אבא שאול's rule refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier clause of the משנה אבא שאול is commenting on.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: which part of the משנה is אבא שאול's rule talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question. It wants to know which earlier ruling in the משנה אבא שאול's general rule is attached to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has more than one clause. One clause forbids waiting at the תחום to hire workers or bring produce. Another clause permits waiting there to guard a field. The גמרא wants to know whether אבא שאול is explaining one of these clauses or adding to it, because that changes what his rule means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was asked of them': the opening of a real question
'On which one?': which clause it refers to

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Abba Shaul, to which [clause does he refer]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the משנה is the context for אבא שאול's general rule.

steps.title: Testing the first option: the clause about hiring workers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that אבא שאול is referring to the first clause, which forbids waiting at the תחום to hire workers or bring produce. It begins to test this idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he is referring to the first clause: 'One may not wait at the edge of the תחום to hire workers or to bring produce' —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out its first possible answer: maybe אבא שאול's rule belongs to the רישא. This is a setup line, and the sentence finishes on the next amud, where the גמרא will challenge this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא says you may not wait at the תחום on שבת in order to hire workers or bring produce once שבת ends. The גמרא checks whether אבא שאול's rule fits as a comment on that clause. The word אילימא ('if you say') usually signals that this option is about to run into a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say': introduces a suggestion that will be tested
The first clause of the משנה
Waiting at the edge of the Shabbat boundary until dark
Workers

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא has decided that the rule refers to the רישא. This is only a suggestion, and it is about to be questioned.

phrases.english: If you say he refers to the first clause:
"One may not wait for nightfall at the boundary
to hire workers or to bring produce" —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the first possible answer to the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tentative suggestion: אבא שאול refers to the רישא about hiring workers and bringing produce. The suggestion is about to be challenged.
